items.summary: Campus Law Centre (CLC), Delhi University's (DU) Team 2 has won the inaugural Law Alumni Golf Championship (LAGC) 2026, held at the Chandigarh Golf Club on September 5. The winning team comprised Ankush Das , Inderbir Singh Alag , Ravi Nanda and Mrinal Bharti . CLC's Team 1, comprising JP Sengh , Sudhanshu Batra , Harkirat Sawhney and Sitesh Mukherjee, finished as first runners-up. National Law University, Delhi (NLUD), represented by Dhruv Gupta , Keerat Dhillon , Akal Brar and Precious Kelson , finished as second runners-up. All three top team positions, in a competition played in the Double Peoria Net format, went to Delhi-based institutions. The championship was organised by the Legal Fairways Foundation in association with DLF. It is being described as India's first inter-law school alumni golf tournament. The inaugural edition drew participation from 18 law schools and universities, bringing together judges, corporate counsel and lawyers from across the country. items.title: Good ideas no longer need a sponsor before they can exist: vibecode.law co-founder Alex Baker
items.summary: The Indian LegalTech Network (ILTN) and vibecode.law have launched the Vibeathon 2026, billed as India’s first “vibe-coding” hackathon for lawyers. The initiative gives lawyers, law students and other legal professionals three weeks to identify problems in legal practice and build working solutions using AI-assisted coding platforms. Participants do not need prior coding experience, with the organisers seeking to demonstrate how AI can lower the barriers to building software for legal practice. vibecode.law, launched earlier this year by Chris Bridges of Tacit Legal, Matt Pollins of Lupl and Alex Baker of Legal Tech Collective, began as a weekend project between its three founders. Baker noted that the platform has since seen hundreds of lawyers from around the world build a wide variety of applications and share them with others exploring legal technology. Baker further spoke about what prompted the creation of vibecode.law, where lawyers should begin if they have never coded before, the limits of AI-built prototypes and what vibe coding could mean for innovation within law firms. items.title: Gujarat to host National Film Awards for first time, breaking decades-old tradition
items.summary: The National Film Awards ceremony is set to leave New Delhi for the first time in decades, with the 72nd edition scheduled to be held at Ekta Nagar in Gujarat’s Narmada district on September 22. The ceremony will mark a rare break from a tradition that has largely kept India’s premier national film awards in New Delhi. There has been at least one notable exception. The University Centenary Auditorium in Madras, now Chennai, hosted the 17th National Film Awards ceremony on November 21, 1970, Indian Express reported. The Union government has not publicly stated the reasons behind the shift of venue. It is notable that among this year’s awardees is filmmaker Aanand L Rai, who won Best Direction in the non-feature category for Statue of Unity–Ekta ka Prateek , a film about the Gujarat landmark, the venue for the event. Moreover, the change in venue comes amidst Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s appeal to the Patidar community in Gujarat to consider organising destination weddings at the Statue of Unity rather than travelling abroad to boost the economy. items.title: At Vizag people’s convention on AI data centres, experts and citizens raise alarm
items.summary: Visakhapatnam and its neighbouring coastal districts will soon host hyperscale AI data centres of at least 6.5 GW capacity, an unprecedented scale in India. As alarm over huge data centres persists world over, how these data centres will affect people’s access to water and power, and the environment and wildlife in the hills and forests near these projects, have become recurring questions on the minds of many Vizag citizens. On September 6, the civic group Stop Vizag Data Centres held what they called India’s first people’s convention on AI data centres. As citizen-led movements, particularly in the United States of America, have successfully halted data centre projects in many areas, scores of people came together opposing the upcoming data centres in north Andhra Pradesh. The convention was held at the Alluri Seetharama Raju Vignana Kendram in Vizag, with discussions and talks led by experts in environment, law, water, and energy security, and rights activists from the city. It was attended by many Vizag residents including students and tech workers. items.summary: Former YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) Rajya Sabha MP V Vijayasai Reddy, who had claimed to quit electoral politics earlier this year after a long association with YS Jagan Mohan Reddy, on Monday, September 7, announced that he would float a new political party in Andhra Pradesh. Vijayasai Reddy said the new party would seek to provide a “viable alternative” to the ruling Telugu Desam Party (TDP), the YSRCP and the Jana Sena Party (JSP). He said its name and other details would be announced after Vijaya Dasami. The details of the proposed party, including its name, organisational structure and leadership, are expected to be announced after Vijaya Dasami. The former MP, once considered one of Jagan’s closest political aides, has undergone a significant political shift since his departure from the YSRCP. Vijayasai Reddy had been associated with Jagan for years and was among the prominent faces of the party in Parliament. He also served as the YSRCP’s national general secretary and was a key strategist for the party. items.summary: The Hyderabad police on Tuesday, September 8, arrested Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) MLCs Thatha Madhusudhan and N Naveen Kumar for allegedly making abusive remarks against Telangana Assembly Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar. The complaint was filed by the Speaker’s Officer on Special Duty (OSD), who alleged that the two MLCs made foul and slanderous remarks against the Speaker while being aware of his Madiga caste identity. According to the complaint, the remarks constitute an offence under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The MLCs were arrested under Section 352 (intentional insult) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), and provisions of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The complaint alleged that Madhusudhan and Naveen Kumar used “malicious”, “unprovoked”, and “profoundly slanderous language” against the Speaker. The alleged incident took place around 9.30 am on Monday, September 7, in the security area of the Telangana Legislative Assembly, when official proceedings were underway. items.title: ‘Waste into wealth’: Bengaluru opens solid waste management centre in Koramangala
items.summary: A Solid Waste Management Learning Centre and several waste-processing facilities were inaugurated in Bengaluru’s Koramangala on Monday, September 7, as part of the government’s efforts to promote scientific waste management and recycling. The facilities were inaugurated by Forest, Ecology and Environment Minister Ramalinga Reddy, Commissioner K N Ramesh and former Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) member Chandrappa. According to the Greater Bengaluru Authority, the learning centre will offer practical training on waste segregation, scientific disposal, recycling and resource recovery. The programme is intended for students, residents of apartment complexes, commercial establishments and civic workers. Among the facilities inaugurated is a 13-tonne-capacity biomethanation plant, which will process organic waste and generate biogas for use by nearby hotels. The site also has 25-tonne-capacity mini transfer stations for handling and transferring waste. Other units at the centre will process different types of waste.
